transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time. I guess I'm here because... well, things at work just got a little out of hand recently? I'm an industrial production manager, so being driven and taking initiative is usually a good thing, right? 

For a little while, I was doing really well—or I thought I was. I was launching all these nonstop plant redesign projects, and I was so focused that I was calling suppliers well after hours... I even rewrote the entire shift plan completely by myself. I just wanted to do a really good job and be proactive, you know? 

But then... um, I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, but I suddenly just couldn't keep up with the very plans I had set in motion. I just sort of stalled out and couldn't do any of it. I feel awful about letting my team down, so I thought I should get some help. Is that... does that make sense as a reason to be here?
Can you tell me approximately how many days in a row you were in that intensely energetic, non-stop working state before you suddenly stalled out?

Um, I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I didn't really keep track of the exact days because, well, I just thought I was having a really productive week. I mean, it's pretty normal to have a few days where you just get a lot done, right? I hope it's okay that I don't have an exact number for you... I just remember it felt like a really good stretch of work before things got overwhelming. Does that help at all, or did you need a specific number?
During that stretch of intense energy and productivity, did you notice you needed much less sleep than usual—like only a few hours—while still feeling rested and energetic?

Um... well, I guess I should admit that I wasn't really sleeping very much. I hope that doesn't sound irresponsible of me. I was maybe getting... two or three hours a night? 

But I promise I felt completely fine! I wasn't dragging or anything. I was showing up at the plant every morning feeling really sharp and charged. It honestly just felt like... well, like sleep was kind of optional? Or just really inefficient when I had so much good work I could be doing for the company. 

I made sure I was still on top of everything during that time, so as long as I was doing a good job, getting by on a little less sleep isn't too concerning, right?
Aside from this recent high-energy period, have you ever had a separate stretch of time—weeks or more—where you felt persistently sad, low on energy, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Um... well, I guess... yes, I have. I hope it's okay to admit that. It's actually been happening recently, after that really productive stretch I mentioned. 

I'm staying in a temporary apartment right now for work, and... lately I just wake up with this really heavy, hollow feeling? It's like the day is already ruined before I even get in the car to drive to the plant. I really try to shake it off, I promise I do, because I want to be a good manager and be there for my team. But it's just been so hard to get going. 

I know everyone gets sad sometimes, so maybe I'm just letting the stress get to me too much? I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or not trying hard enough... does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about?
During this recent low period, have you had any thoughts of hopelessness so intense that you've thought about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Um... no, no, I haven't had thoughts like that. I mean, I know things have felt really heavy lately, but I would never want to do anything to hurt myself. I hope you don't think I'm that unstable... I'm really just trying to push through this slump and get back to being productive. 

I know life is worth living, and I have a lot of responsibilities at the plant that I take really seriously. It's just... a little harder to see the bright side right now, I guess? But I promise I'm keeping it together. I wouldn't do anything drastic. Is it okay that I'm just feeling a bit down, but not... you know, not in a dangerous way?
How many days or weeks has this heavy, low feeling been going on so far?

Um... well, it's been a little while now. I hope it doesn't sound like I've just been letting myself go for too long, but... I guess it's been about three months that I've been feeling this way? 

It really started to set in around the time I had to move into this temporary apartment for the new plant assignment. I really want to do a good job here, but being away from home and trying to manage everything at the plant... it's just made it a lot harder to shake this feeling off. 

I'm still showing up every day, though! I haven't missed any work. I'm trying my best to manage it on my own, but it's just been dragging on a bit longer than I'd like. Is three months... is that a normal amount of time to feel like this when you're under a lot of stress at work?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a distinct period of elevated, goal-directed activity with decreased need for sleep (2-3 hours) without fatigue, increased productivity, and impulsive decision-making (unilaterally rewriting shift plans, after-hours calls) consistent with a hypomanic/manic episode. This was followed by a subsequent, distinct depressive episode lasting approximately 3 months characterized by low mood, anhedonia-like heaviness, and low energy, without suicidal ideation and with preserved functioning (still attending work). The presence of both a manic/hypomanic episode and a current depressive episode of moderate severity (functioning maintained, no psychotic features, no active suicidality) meets criteria for Bipolar Affective Disorder, current episode moderate depression (F31.3), rather than unipolar depression (F32.1) given the clear preceding manic-like period, or severe bipolar depression (F31.4/F31.5) given preserved functioning and absence of suicidal ideation or psychotic features.
